compare.intro: This unit's points come in look-alike sets: はじめる is a planned or gradual start and だす a sudden one; つづける is an action that keeps going, っぱなし is something left that way (usually a complaint), and ている only describes the state; かける and かけの stop halfway, きる goes all the way to the end, and きれない cannot get there; たまま keeps a state as it is, ずに is plain 'without', and ないで is 'without' that can also end a request like ください or ほしい.

forms.tag: そのまま（よくない） · left that way, a complaint
forms.ja: [昨日|きのう]は一日中、[会議|かいぎ]で[座|すわ]り{っぱなし}でした。
forms.en: Yesterday I was sitting in meetings all day long.

forms.tag: その状態で · in the same state
forms.ja: 時間がなくて、立った{まま}おにぎりを食べました。
forms.en: I had no time, so I ate a rice ball standing up.

forms.ja: [辞書|じしょ]を使わ{ずに}、[新聞|しんぶん]が読めるようになりました。
forms.en: I can now read the newspaper without using a dictionary.

check.label: Not even once
check.q: ^一度も^（　　）、山の上まで[登|のぼ]りました。
why: っぱなし is a state that goes on and on, often a complaint. Resting the whole time does not get you to the top, and 一度も needs a negative.
たまま keeps a state going while something else happens. 休んだまま is positive, but 一度も needs a negative.
一度も + a negative: not resting even once. 休まずに means without resting, and the main action [登|のぼ]りました follows.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: ^来週から^、新しい[教科書|きょうかしょ]を（　　）^[予定|よてい]^です。
why: だす is a sudden start that nobody planned. It does not go with [予定|よてい], a planned start.
きる means using something until nothing is left. 来週から gives a starting point, not an end.
A planned start from next week: 使いはじめる, and [予定|よてい] shows it is planned.
かける means starting and stopping halfway. Nobody plans that, and it does not fit 来週から.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: [隣|となり]の[部屋|へや]の人が^朝から夕方まで^ピアノを（　　）、勉強ができませんでした。
why: The playing went on from morning to evening: ひき[続|つづ]けて. That is why the speaker could not study.
だす marks only the moment the playing began. 朝から夕方まで needs an action that goes on.
かける means starting and stopping halfway. Here the playing went on all day.
きる means playing something, such as one piece, right to the end. It says nothing about the playing going on all day.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: ^人が多すぎて^、[全員|ぜんいん]はこの[会議室|かいぎしつ]に（　　）。
why: かける means starting and stopping halfway. 多すぎて gives a reason something cannot be done, and [全員|ぜんいん]は (not all of them) needs a negative.
はじめます is a start. [全員|ぜんいん]は (not all of them) needs a negative, and 多すぎて gives a reason something cannot be done.
ずにいる means staying without doing something, by choice. Here the room is too small, so the point is that they cannot.
There are too many people, so not all of them can get in: 入りきれません.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: ^暑い日は^、子どもを車の中に（　　）、買い物に行かないでください。
why: ずに means without: don't go shopping without leaving the child in the car. That is the opposite of the warning.
The child stays in the car, left as it is, while you go shopping: [残|のこ]したまま.
きる is for doing all of something to the end. Leaving a child in a car is not that kind of action.
かける means starting and stopping halfway. Leaving a child in a car is not done halfway.

drill.label: Build the sentence
drill.hint: 急に goes with a sudden start. Which tile says how long the barking went on?
drill.full: 夜中に急に{ほえだした}犬が朝までほえ[続|つづ]けました。
drill.explain: 急に, ほえだした, 犬が, 朝まで. 急にほえだした describes 犬: it suddenly started barking (だす). 朝まで goes with ほえ[続|つづ]けました: it kept on barking until morning (つづける).

drill.label: Build the sentence
drill.hint: かけの needs a noun right after it. What did the speaker leave without finishing?
drill.full: [昨日|きのう]は、{やりかけの}仕事を終わらせずに帰ってしまいました。
drill.explain: やりかけの, 仕事を, 終わらせずに, 帰って. やりかけの describes 仕事: work started and left half-done. 終わらせずに means without finishing it, and 帰って joins しまいました.

exam.label: Choose the form
exam.q: 使ったはさみをテーブルの上に（　　）にしないで、元の場所に戻してください。
exam.explain: っぱなしにする: leaving the scissors out after use, which the speaker does not like, so they ask for them to be put back. つづける is for an action that keeps going, and scissors lying on a table are a state, not an action. 出しかけ would mean starting to take them out and stopping. 出しきる means taking out all of something, which does not fit one pair of scissors left on a table.

exam.label: Choose the form
exam.q: 夜遅くに電話を（　　）ほしいと、母に言われた。
exam.explain: ないでほしい: the mother asked the speaker not to call late at night. ずに means without and joins two actions; it cannot come before ほしい. かけたまま and かけっぱなしで describe a state left as it is, and neither can be followed by ほしい here.

exam.label: Build the sentence
exam.full: 友だちに借りた本を最後まで{読みきれない}まま返してしまった。
exam.explain: 最後まで, 読みきれない, まま, 返して. 最後まで goes with 読みきれない: the speaker could not read it to the end. ないまま says the book was still unfinished when it went back, and 返して joins しまった.

scene.en: The rules board at a public swimming pool
scene.intro: Tap each word on the board that tells swimmers what they may and may not do.

check.label: How the exam asks it
check.q: プールサイドを走るのは_危険_です。
check.explain: 危険, danger, is きけん: 危 キ (dangerous) and 険 ケン (risky). きげん wrongly makes け voiced, ぎけん wrongly makes き voiced, and きっけん adds a small つ that this word does not have.

skill.ask: Which rules on the board apply to Yang, and what must Yang do before going into the pool?
skill.passage:
市民プールをご利用のみなさまへ
①^はじめてご利用になる方は、受付で利用カードを作ってください^。二回目からは、受付でカードを見せるだけでかまいません。
②^プールに入る前に、シャワーを浴びてください^。
③水泳ぼうしを必ずかぶってください。^お持ちでない方には、受付で貸し出します^（一回百円）。
④^めがねをかけたままプールに入らないでください^。水泳用のゴーグルはかまいません。
⑤小学三年生までのお子さんは、大人といっしょに入ってください。
⑥プールサイドを走ったり、飛び込んだりしないでください。たいへん危険です。
skill.strategy: Check Yang against each rule in turn: is this the first visit, is there a cap, and does Yang wear glasses?

item.q: ヤンさんは、今日はじめてこのプールに来ました。水着と水泳ぼうしは持ってきました。ふだんはめがねをかけています。ヤンさんがプールに入る前にしなければならないことはどれか。
options: 利用カードを作り、ぼうしを借りて、シャワーを浴びる。
めがねをはずして、シャワーを浴びる。
利用カードを作り、めがねをはずして、シャワーを浴びる。
利用カードを作り、シャワーを浴びる。めがねはかけたままでいい。
short: カード、めがね、シャワー
item.explain: Today is Yang's first visit, so rule ① applies: make a card at the desk. Everyone must shower first (rule ②). Yang wears glasses, so rule ④ applies: take them off before going in. Yang brought a cap, so there is no need to borrow one.
why: Yang brought a swimming cap, so there is no need to borrow one (rule ③). Taking off the glasses (rule ④) is also missing.
Today is Yang's first visit, so Yang must also make a card at the desk (rule ①).
Rule ④ says not to go into the pool wearing glasses. Only swimming goggles are allowed.
